correctness.rationale: For m,n>=2 and 0<epsilon<1 with self-weight 1+epsilon, integer neighbor sums of either part at most -2 or at least +2 overwrite its opposite part unanimously; sums -1,0,1 preserve the original spins. Hence exactly the low/central/high trichotomy, its nine pair cases, frozen central+central, alternating low+high, all-plus high/no-low and all-minus low/no-high. By step 2 the system is on its final orbit; no tie ambiguity arises. Independent literal synchronous spin updates (not reuse of supplied checker) matched outcomes on all 16+128+256+1024+1024 assignments for (m,n)=(2,2),(3,4),(4,4),(5,5),(6,4). Independence of initial binomial counts implies the four rational finite basin probabilities; unbiased central binomial mass has parity factors 1 or 2 and the triangular-array CLT at p=.5+u/sqrt(m+n) yields the displayed Phi Gaussian crossover. The 2-step bound is only for these complete bipartite and exact self-weight assumptions.

value.rationale: Complete bipartite networks are canonical two-community interacting models and the NCO self-retention rule makes frozen disagreement mathematically distinct from the two-cycle. The exact all-initial-condition classification and finite-size probability formulas show a nonzero limiting 1/2 chance of bipartition alternation at unbiased initialization, parity-dependent frozen fractions and a sharp sqrt(N) bias window. This is a motivated full classification and nontrivial probabilistic scaling law, not a random tiny case.
